examples.question_text: Four valid cuts in a road network have capacities $C_1=46$, $C_2=38$, $C_3=43$ and $C_4=38$ vehicles per minute. These cuts include a minimum cut. Identify the minimum cuts and determine the maximum traffic flow.
examples.solution_text:
$\min(46,38,43,38)=38$.

Both $C_2$ and $C_4$ are minimum cuts. By the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem, the maximum traffic flow is $38\text{ vehicles/min}$.

examples.question_text: Path saturation establishes a maximum flow of $64\text{ kL/h}$ in a water network. Two valid cuts have capacities $K=73\text{ kL/h}$ and $M=64\text{ kL/h}$. Determine whether each cut is a minimum cut, giving reasons.
examples.solution_text:
The minimum cut capacity equals the established maximum flow, $64\text{ kL/h}$.

Cut $K$ is not minimum because $73>64$.

Cut $M$ is minimum because its capacity equals the maximum flow.

examples.question_text: A valid cut crosses three edges directed from the source side to the sink side with capacities $42$, $36$ and $27\text{ L/s}$. It also crosses an edge directed back towards the source side with capacity $15\text{ L/s}$. No other cut capacities or attainable flows are known. Calculate the cut capacity and explain what can be concluded about the maximum flow.
examples.solution_text:
Exclude the reverse edge.

$\text{Cut capacity}=42+36+27=105\text{ L/s}$.

Every valid cut gives an upper bound, so the maximum flow is at most $105\text{ L/s}$. Equality requires proof that this cut is minimum, such as an attainable flow of $105\text{ L/s}$.

coverage.summary: Added four worked examples covering all seven distinct assessed methods. The network example includes editable question and solution diagrams, reverse-edge exclusion, exhaustive cut comparison, an attainable matching flow and saturation. Solutions use editable prose and inline mathematics with automatic blue styling. No assessment content was changed or re-audited; final-size diagram verification remains for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: Comparing 46, 38, 43 and 38 gives minimum capacity 38. Since the candidates include a minimum cut, C2 and C4 are minimum cuts and maximum flow is 38 vehicles/min.

The four source-side sets {S}, {S,A}, {S,B} and {S,A,B} give capacities 21, 19, 21 and 15 respectively. For {S,A}, BA crosses backwards and is excluded. The minimum cut consists of AT and BT; the red line separates these edges from T. Sending 7 along SAT and 8 along SBT respects SA≤9 and SB≤12, conserves flow at A and B, and attains 15 L/min. AT and BT each have zero unused capacity.
The established maximum flow fixes the minimum cut capacity at 64 kL/h. K has capacity 73>64 and is not minimum; valid cut M has capacity 64 and is minimum.

Only forward capacities count: 42+36+27=105 L/s. The reverse capacity 15 is excluded. This valid cut proves maximum flow≤105 L/s; equality remains unestablished without minimum-cut or matching attainable-flow evidence.
